# Introduction {#sec:introduction}

This vignette demonstrates how to generate structured,
publication-ready figures using GTAPViz’s built-in visualization
tools.

The visualization framework is based on the **`SL4File`** and
**`HARFile`** sheets, which define the variables and figure titles
used for plotting. Users can specify these directly within an external
mapping file or generate them dynamically in the R environment.

# Loading Package

Before proceeding, ensure that `GTAPViz` and `HARplus` are installed
and loaded:

```{r package, eval = FALSE}
library(GTAPViz)
```

**Note:** If the required packages are not yet installed, please refer
to:

-   [GTAPViz](https://github.com/Bodysbobb/GTAPViz)

-   [HARplus](https://github.com/Bodysbobb/HARplus)

# Package Overview {#sec:package-overview}

This package facilitates the reporting of CGE model outputs,
particularly for GTAP users, but it can also be applied to other
results based on `.har` and `.sl4` files. Its primary function is to
generate [Figures](#sec:figure-type) and [Tables](#sec:report-table).
Additionally, several [useful tools](#sec:additional-utilities) are
available for data manipulation to enhance figure illustration.

# Figure Types {#sec:figure-type}

This package introduces four different plot commands that can generate
more than 10 different plots:

1. [`comparison_plot`](#sec:comparisonplot): Compares *variables* across all experiments for *selected observations from a selected dimension* (e.g., region, sector). Examples: `qgdp`, `ppriv`, `EV`.

2. [`detail_plot`](#sec:detailplot): Visualizes *a variable* across *all or selected observations from one or two dimensions* for each experiment. Examples: `qo`, `qxw`, `qmw`.

3. [`macro_plot`](#sec:macroplot): Shows global macroeconomic indicators or data *without dimensions*, with each experiment as *a single aggregated value*. Examples: `pgdpwld`, `qgdpwld`, `vgdpwld`.

4. [`stack_plot`](#sec:stackplot): Displays the *composition* of a variable for decomposition analysis, such as `EV` decomposition from GTAP results.


# Report Tables {#sec:report-table}

This package provides a single command for generating several pivot
tables designed for academic presentations. This vignette provides
some examples in [Creating Report Table](#sec:report-table-creating).

1.  [`Comparison Table`](#sec:comparison-table)
2.  [`GTAP Macro Table`](#sec:macro-table)
3.  [`Detail Table`](#sec:detail-table)
4.  [`Decomposition Table`](#sec:decomp-table)

# Project Directory {#sec:project-setting}

To use this R code, all solution files, including `.sl4` and `.har`,
must be saved from RUNGTAP or CMD and *placed in the same folder*.

Adjust the `<project.folder>` directory to your desired path:

```{r Project Folder, eval = FALSE}
project.folder <- "your/folder/path"

# Optional: You might not need to adjust this
input.folder <- paste0(project.folder, "/in") 
map.folder <- paste0(project.folder, "/map")      
output.folder <- paste0(project.folder, "/out")   
```

By default, this R code assumes that `<project.folder>` contains the
following three main folders:

```         
├── 📂 out/ 
```
:::

# Mapping Folder {#sec:mapping-folder}

The mapping XLSX template is available here: [OutputMapping.xlsx](https://github.com/Bodysbobb/GTAPViz/tree/main/inst/extdata/map). It contains three main sheets: *SL4File*, *HARFile*, and *FilterData*.


## SL4File and HARFile Sheets {#sec:main-sheets}

• *"Variable"* specifies the required variable from each file.

• *"Description"* is optional for defining variables and plot titles.

• *"Unit"* is *required* for all figure commands.


**Note:** The *Description* and *Unit* columns can be left empty if using [GTAP defaults](#sec:info.mode).

You can import your external mapping file into R using the following
method:

```{r Mapping File, eval = FALSE}
sl4map <- readxl::read_xlsx(map.folder, sheet = "SL4File")
harmap <- readxl::read_xlsx(map.folder, sheet = "HARFile")
```

**Note:** You can name the file anything, but you must adjust the function accordingly. In this vignette, `.sl4` and `.har` mappings are named "sl4map" and "harmap," respectively.


Below is an example of mapping file:

<div style="font-family: monospace; background-color: #282C34; color: #ABB2BF; padding: 10px; border-radius: 5px; width: fit-content;">
  <table style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%;">
    <tr>
      <th style="border: 1px solid #ABB2BF; padding: 8px; text-align: left;">Variable</th>
      <th style="border: 1px solid #ABB2BF; padding: 8px; text-align: left;">Description</th>
      <th style="border: 1px solid #ABB2BF; padding: 8px; text-align: left;">Unit</th>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="border: 1px solid #ABB2BF; padding: 8px;">qgdp</td>
      <td style="border: 1px solid #ABB2BF; padding: 8px;">Real GDP Index (%)</td>
      <td style="border: 1px solid #ABB2BF; padding: 8px;">percent</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="border: 1px solid #ABB2BF; padding: 8px;">EV</td>
      <td style="border: 1px solid #ABB2BF; padding: 8px;">Welfare Equivalents</td>
      <td style="border: 1px solid #ABB2BF; padding: 8px;">million USD</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td style="border: 1px solid #ABB2BF; padding: 8px;">pprive</td>
      <td style="border: 1px solid #ABB2BF; padding: 8px;">Consumer Price Index</td>
      <td style="border: 1px solid #ABB2BF; padding: 8px;">percent</td>
    </tr>
  </table>
</div>


💡 **Tip:** The [mapping file](https://github.com/Bodysbobb/GTAPViz/tree/main/inst/extdata/map) can be manually created in R as a dataframe. It must include at least the *"Variable"* column, while *"Description"* and *"Unit"* are optional based on the selected [info.mode](#sec:info.mode).  

For example, the following R code creates an equivalent mapping dataframe:

```{r Munual Mapping File Create, eval=FALSE}
mapping_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = c("qgdp", "EV", "ppriv"),
  Description = c("Real GDP Index", "Welfare Equivalents", "Consumer Price Index"),
  Unit = c("Percent", "million USD", "percent"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```


## FilterData Sheet {#sec:filterdata-sheets}

This sheet is optional and can be defined in R instead. It contains two columns for *filtering data from the dataframe*. Leave it empty to include all entries.

• *"Region"* excludes specified regions by filtering the "REG" column in all dataframes.  
• *"Sector"* excludes specified sectors by filtering the "COMM" and "ACTS" columns in all dataframes.  

**Note:** These columns also determine the sorting order. See [Sorting Output](#sec:sorting-output) for details.  


# R Environment Configuration {#sec:r-setup}

This section configures experiment names, description and unit handling, and output formats for processing GTAP model results.

## 1. Experiment Names {#sec:experiment-name}

Define `<experiment>` to specify *input* file names. The experiment name:  

• Appears in plots and is added to the *"Experiment"* column. While renaming files within R is possible using [rename value](#sec:rename-value), manual renaming the input file name is recommended.  

• Sorts figures and tables based on the order of `<experiment>`. See [Sorting Output](#sec:sorting-output) for details.  

• **Important:** `.har` input files must include "-WEL" in their names. If unsure, refer to the [input folder figure](#sec:input-folder). 

The following command processes the files and sorts the output with EXP1 before EXP2:

- `EXP1.sl4` and `EXP1-WEL.har`  
- `EXP2.sl4` and `EXP2-WEL.har`  

```{r Experiment Name, eval = FALSE}
experiment <- c("EXP1", "EXP2")
```

**Note:** You can include as many experiments (inputs) as needed, but a higher
number will increase processing time.


## 2. Description and Unit Handling {#sec:info.mode}

Controls how the `"Description"` and `"Unit"` columns are included in the output:

- `"Yes"`   → Uses descriptions and units from the mapping file.  
- `"No"`    → Excludes `"Description"` and `"Unit"`.  
- `"GTAPv7"`→ Applies default definitions and units from *GTAP Model Version 7*.  
- `"Mix"`   → Uses manual values when available; otherwise, applies GTAP defaults.  

```{r Information Structure, eval = FALSE}
info.mode <- "Mix"
```

**Note:** GTAP defaults apply only to variables included in the GTAPv7 model. Any additional variables must be manually defined.


## 3. Output Formats {#sec:output-formats}

Select the required output formats (`"Yes"` = export, `"No"` = skip):  

- *CSV (`csv.output`)* → `"No"`  
- *STATA (`stata.output`)* → `"No"`  
- *R (`r.output`)* → `"Yes"`  
- *Text (`txt.output`)* → `"Yes"`  

You can also choose to export only the organized raw data, with or without visualization, by setting `plot_data` to `TRUE` or `FALSE`.  

The following command exports all formats and generates data for plotting:  

```{r Output Formats, eval = FALSE}
csv.output <- "YES"    
stata.output <- "YES"  
r.output <- "YES"
txt.output <- "YES"   

plot_data = TRUE
```

## R Configuration Summary {#sec:r-config-summary}

In summary, the entire R setup is captured in the following chunk:  

```{r Config Summary, eval = FALSE}
# 1. Project Directory
project.folder <- "your/project/folder"

# 2. Define the Input Names 
experiment <- c("US_All", "US_All_RetalTar")

# 3. Adding Description / Unit (Yes/No/GTAPv7/Mix)
info.mode <- "Mix"

# 4. Choosing Output: (CSV, STATA, R, TEXT) 
csv.output <- "No"    
stata.output <- "No"  
r.output <- "No"
txt.output <- "No"   

# 5. For Plotting: (TRUE/FALSE)
plot_data = TRUE
```

💡 **Tip:** Once this process is complete, no further modifications are needed—provided the project folder and mapping file format remain unchanged.  


# Output Sorting Rules {#sec:sorting-output}

This automated process determines the display order of three datasets based on predefined lists:  
• *Experiment* is sorted according to the order in `<experiment>`, affecting the sequence of experiment panels in plots.  
• *Region* is sorted based on the "Region" column in the *FilterData* sheet, determining the order of regions in figures and tables.  
• *Sector* is sorted according to the "Sector" column in the *FilterData* sheet, controlling the arrangement of sectors in outputs.  

To customize sorting for additional columns, manual adjustments may be required.  

### Example:  
- selected_regions <- c("USA", "CHN"), USA will appear before CHN in the comparison figure. 

- experiment <- c("EXP2", "EXP1"), the EXP2 panel will appear before EXP1 (e.g., from left to right in a figure).  


# Input Data Preparation {#sec:input-preparation}

## 1. Setting Up Sub-Directorie {#sec:subdirectory}

You can run the following code without modification if you followed all the previous instructions:

```{r Default Input, eval = FALSE}
# Default Folder
input.folder <- paste0(project.folder, "/in")
map.folder <- paste0(project.folder, "/map")
output.folder <- paste0(project.folder, "/out")

# Default Mapping File
sl4map <- readxl::read_xlsx(paste0(map.folder, "/OutputMapping.xlsx"), sheet = "SL4File")
harmap <- readxl::read_xlsx(paste0(map.folder, "/OutputMapping.xlsx"), sheet = "HARFile")
filter.map <- readxl::read_xlsx(paste0(map.folder, "/OutputMapping.xlsx"), sheet = "FilterData")
```

If you're familiar with R, you can customize it, but some function adjustments may be needed.  


## 2. Data Filtering Setup {#sec:filtering-data}

This filtering process runs automatically when the mapping file is used as instructed. However, experienced users can define it manually in the R environment:  

```{r Filtering Data, eval = FALSE}
selected_regions <- if(length(filter.map$Region) > 0) filter.map$Region else NULL
selected_sector  <- if(length(filter.map$Sector) > 0) filter.map$Sector else NULL
```

💡 **Tip:** If the plot is too dense or unclear, try filtering more data!  


## 3. GTAP Data Extraction {#sec:automategtap}

To streamline figure generation from GTAP results, I developed an automated data extraction method using the following command:  

```{r Preparing Data for Plot, eval = FALSE}
process_gtap_data(
  sl4var = sl4map, 
  harvar = harmap,
  sl4map = sl4map,
  harmap = harmap,
  region_select = selected_regions,
  sector_select = selected_sector,
  subtotal = FALSE,
  experiment = experiment, 
  mapping_info = info.mode,
  project_dir = project.folder,
  plot_data = plot_data,
  output_formats = list(
    "csv" = csv.output,
    "stata" = stata.output,
    "rds" = r.output,
    "txt" = txt.output))
```

**Note:**  
For non-GTAP models or manual data extraction, see [Manual Data Processing](#sec:manualdata).  

💡 **Tip:** 
This automation uses the `"HARplus::group_data_by_dims"` command. However, other formats, such as `"HARplus::get_data_by_var"`, `"HARplus::get_data_by_dims"`, or custom data formats, can also be used with the figure code with some modifications.  


## 4. Converting Units and Labels (Optional) {#sec:custom-unit}

These optional but recommended steps improve figure clarity. Use the following code to convert million USD to billion USD after data extraction:  

```{r Optional Convert Unit, eval = FALSE}
sl4.plot.data <- convert_units(sl4.plot.data, 
                               scale_auto = "mil2bil")

har.plot.data <- convert_units(har.plot.data, 
                               scale_auto = "bil2mil")
```

**Note:** This function supports various unit conversions, while `scale_auto` simplifies common conversions such as mil2bil, bil2mil, pct2frac, and frac2pct. You can define custom conversions manually—see [Converting Units](#sec:converting-unit) or `"?convert_units"` for details. 


::: alert
# **Important: Before Starting the Plot**

## **Rule of Thumb**

You can freely modify and rename most columns and values in the dataframe, as long as you adjust the corresponding commands.  

*However, avoid renaming "Experiment", "Value", and "Variable" before using the plot function.* Instead, use the plot function options to rename them if needed. 


## **Practical Example**

The plot structure depends on how *`x_axis_from`*, *`split_by`*, *`compare_by_experiment`*, and *`invert_panel`* are set.  

- *compare_by_experiment = FALSE* → Plots are grouped by *split_by*, with experiments as panels.  
- *compare_by_experiment = TRUE* → Plots are grouped by *experiment*, with *split_by* as panels.  
- *invert_panel = FALSE* → Panels separate experiments or regions.  

- *invert_panel = TRUE* → Panels separate variables instead.  

For example, setting:
- *x_axis_from = "Region"*, *split_by = "Variable"*, and *compare_by_experiment = FALSE*  
  → Creates a separate plot for each variable, with regions on the x-axis and experiments as panels.


## **Tip on Plot Dimension**

Plot functions do not allow direct font size adjustments. To optimize the figure, adjust:  

- *panel_rows*, *panel_cols* → Controls the number of panel rows and columns.  
- *width*, *height* → Defines the exported figure dimensions, which can indirectly adjust font size.  

The command defaults to a balanced square layout, but tweaking these settings can improve the output.  

## **Final Tip**  

Experiment with these options to customize your visualization! For details on all plots, see: `<?comparison_plot>`, `<?macro_plot>`, `<?detail_plot>`, `<?stack_plot>`.  

:::


# Comparison Plot {#sec:comparisonplot}

This figure compares one or multiple *variables* across all experiments for *selected observations from a chosen dimension* (e.g., region, sector).  

### Key Features:
- Supports only two dimensions for plotting.  

- Displays all selected variables in one plot, making it ideal for a few observations; too many can make it dense and unclear.  

- Designed for comparing selected variables across experiments.  

💡 **Tip:** To check which data is compatible, use `"HARplus::group_data_by_dims"`. Variables listed under the `"1D"` sublist are suitable.  

### Practical Examples  

Plotting `qgdp`, `ppriv`, `EV`, `tot`, and `u` generates six separate figures using the following command:  

```{r Comparison Plot, eval = FALSE}
region.dta <- sl4.plot.data[["1D"]][["Region"]]

comparison_plot(region.dta,
                x_axis_from = "Region",
                split_by = "Variable",
                plot_var = sl4map,
                title_prefix = "Impact on",
                output_dir = output.folder,
                var_name_by_description = TRUE,
                compare_by_experiment = FALSE,
                invert_panel = FALSE,
                separate_figure = FALSE,
                color_tone = "purdue",
                panel_rows = NULL,
                panel_cols = NULL,
                width = 20,
                height = 12,
                legend_position = "bottom")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="600px"}
knitr::include_graphics("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bodysbobb/GTAPViz/main/vignettes/images/cpsplot.png")
```


# GTAP Macro Variable Plot {#sec:macroplot}

This figure displays aggregated values across all experiments, typically for global economic impacts. It is designed for GTAP Macro variables extracted from the *"Macros"* header in `<.sl4>` files.  

### Key Features:

- Compares macroeconomic indicators across experiments.  

- Works with aggregated data, making it ideal for global-scale analysis.  

- Primarily used for GTAP Macro variables but can be applied to other aggregated datasets.  

💡 *Tip:* If you have not imported the GTAP Macro data please see [GTAP Macro Data Extraction](#sec:gtapmacro-dataextract)
 
To generate this figure, extract the required GTAP Macro variables (if not already imported) using the `<gtap_macros_data>` command: 


```{r GTAP Macro Plot Data, eval = FALSE}
Macros <- gtap_macros_data(
  input_dir = input.folder,
  experiment_names = experiment,
  subtotal_level = FALSE
)
```

If you want to specifically only some variables within the GTAP Macros
to be plotted as well as to rename those variable, you can do as the
follows in R environment:

```{r GTAP Macro Plot Data Rename, eval = FALSE}
# Selecting Variables
selected_marcro <- c("pgdpwld", "qgdpwld", "vgdpwld")
macros_new_name <- c("pgdpwld", "qgdpwld", "vgdpwld")

# Rename
macro.map <- data.frame(
  Variable = selected_marcro,
  Description = macros_new_name,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

To plot this figure, you can use the following command:

```{r GTAP Macro Plot, eval = FALSE}
macro_plot(Macros,
           plot_var = macro.map,
           compare_by_experiment = FALSE,
           color_tone = "grey",
           output_dir = output.folder,
           var_name_by_description = FALSE,
           panel_rows = 2,
           width = 45,
           separate_figure = FALSE,
           legend_position = "bottom")

```


```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="600px"}
knitr::include_graphics("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bodysbobb/GTAPViz/main/vignettes/images/GTAPMacros.png")
```

# Detail Plot {#sec:detailplot}

This figure visualizes large-scale data, displaying all sectors (*COMM*, *ACTS*) or all regions (*REG*) within each experiment.  

### Key Features:
- Supports visualization across two selected dimensions.  
- Suitable for datasets too large for *comparison_plot*.  
- Automatically detects and aligns variables with different dimension names.  
- Filters data by selecting the most affected variables using *top_impact*.  

💡 *Tip:* To check compatible variables, use `"HARplus::group_data_by_dims"`. Variables in the `"2D"` sublist are best suited for this figure.  

For example, the following command plots all variables with sectors on the y-axis for each region:  

```{r Detail Plot, eval = FALSE}
twod.dta <- sl4.plot.data[["2D"]]
lapply(twod.dta, function(df) {
  detail_plot(df,
              y_axis_from = c("Sector"),
              split_by = "Region",
              plot_var = sl4map,
              output_dir = output.folder,
              var_name_by_description = TRUE,
              top_impact = 10,
              panel_rows = 1,
              panel_cols = NULL,
              separate_figure = FALSE,
              invert_panel = FALSE,
              width = 50)})
```

```{r detail plot, echo=FALSE, out.width="600px"}
knitr::include_graphics("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bodysbobb/GTAPViz/main/vignettes/images/detail_plot.png")
```

```{r detail plot top impact, echo=FALSE, out.width="600px"}
knitr::include_graphics("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bodysbobb/GTAPViz/main/vignettes/images/detail_plot_top10.png")
```


# Decomposition (Stack) Plot {#sec:stackplot}

This plot visualizes decomposition results, showing how different components contribute to a total value, making it particularly suitable for decomposition analysis.  

### Key Features:
- Displays the contribution of components to a total value.  
- Allows further decomposition by unstacking components instead of using a stacked bar.  
- Suitable for *welfare decomposition, trade decomposition, and other GTAP structural breakdowns*.  

💡 *Tip:* Since decomposition data often contains multiple components, *renaming and restructuring* may be necessary before plotting.  

For example, the following command renames the welfare component values in the original *"COLUMN"* before plotting:  

```{r Decomposition Plot, eval = FALSE}
# Rename Value if needed
wefare.decomp.rename <- data.frame(
  ColumnName = "COLUMN",
  OldName = c("alloc_A1", "ENDWB1", "tech_C1", "pop_D1", "pref_G1", "tot_E1", "IS_F1"),
  NewName = c("Alloc Eff.", "Endwb", "Tech Chg.", "Pop", "Perf", "ToT", "I-S"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

har.plot.data <- rename_value(har.plot.data, mapping.file = wefare.decomp.rename)
har.plot.data[["A"]][["Variable"]] <- "Welfare"

# Define Decomposition
stack_plot(data = har.plot.data[["A"]],
          x_axis_from = "REG",
          stack_value_from = "COLUMN",
          title_prefix = "",
          output_dir = output.folder,
          separate_figure = FALSE,
          color_tone = "green",
          width = 30,
          height = 15,
          legend_position = "bottom",
          show_total = TRUE,
          unstack_plot = TRUE,
          var_name_by_description = TRUE)

```

```{r stack plot, echo=FALSE, out.width="600px"}
knitr::include_graphics("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bodysbobb/GTAPViz/main/vignettes/images/stack_plot.png")
```



# Creating Report Table {#sec:report-table-creating}

This command generates multiple table formats suitable for *academic presentations* with minimal adjustments. You can process multiple data frames in the same session, even with different pivot formats, but each must be defined separately. See the sample code for details.  

This vignette provides a few examples, but for full usage, refer to `<?report_table>`. 

### Key parameters include:  

-   **`pivot_col`**\
    A named list specifying the column to pivot into wide format.\
-   **`group_by`**\
    A list or character vector defining grouping columns.\
-   **`total_column`**\
    If `TRUE`, adds a “Total” column that sums all numeric columns
    row-wise.\
-   **`separate_file`**\
    If `TRUE`, exports each data frame to its own Excel file;
    otherwise, all go into one workbook.
-   **`include_units`**\
    If `TRUE`, retains the “Unit” column in the grouping
    (recommended).\
-   **`component_exclude`**\
    A vector of component names to exclude (i.e., values in
    `pivot_col` that should be omitted).\
-   **`rename_cols`**\
    A named list mapping old column names to new names.\
-   **`var_name_by_description`**\
    If `TRUE`, names pivoted columns using “Description” (if
    available).\
-   **`add_var_info`**\
    If `TRUE`, appends the variable name to its description in
    parentheses.\
-   **`decimal`**\
    Sets the number of decimal places in output.\
-   **`unit_select`**\
    Keeps only rows matching the specified unit.\
-   **`separate_sheet_by`**\
    Splits the output into multiple sheets by this column.\
-   **`subtotal_level`**\
    If `TRUE`, applies subtotal-based filtering where applicable.\
-   **`repeat_label`**\
    If `TRUE`, repeats all labels in every row (i.e., raw dataset
    style).\
-   **`add_group_line`**\
    Places a border line to separate groups based on the first column.

**Note:**\
- Variable names in the columns cannot be changed here. To rename them
(e.g., country names), do so before invoking this function (see
[Renaming Values in a Dataframe](#sec:rename-value)).

## 1. Comparison Table {#sec:comparison-table}

```{r Comparison Table, eval = FALSE}
report_table(
  data_list = sl4.plot.data[["1D"]],
  pivot_col = list(Region = "Variable"),
  group_by =  list(
    Region = list("Experiment", "Region")),
  rename_cols = list("Experiment" = "Scenario"),
  
  total_column = FALSE,
  decimal = 4,
  subtotal_level = FALSE,
  repeat_label = FALSE,
  include_units = TRUE,

  var_name_by_description = FALSE,
  add_var_info = FALSE,
  add_group_line = FALSE,

  separate_sheet_by = NULL,
  export_table = TRUE,
  output_dir = output.folder,
  separate_file = FALSE,
  workbook_name = "comparison"
)
```

## 2. GTAP Macro Table {#sec:macro-table}

```{r GTAP Macro Table, eval = FALSE}
GTAPMacro <- list(GTAPMacro = Macros)

report_table(
  data_list = GTAPMacro,
  pivot_col = list(
    GTAPMacro = "Experiment"),
  group_by =  list(
    GTAPMacro = list("Variable")),
  rename_cols = list("Experiment" = "Scenario"),
  
  total_column = FALSE,
  decimal = 4,
  subtotal_level = FALSE,
  repeat_label = FALSE,
  include_units = TRUE,

  var_name_by_description = FALSE,
  add_var_info = FALSE,
  add_group_line = FALSE,

  separate_sheet_by = NULL,
  export_table = TRUE,
  output_dir = output.folder,
  separate_file = FALSE,
  workbook_name = "GTAPMacro"
)
```

## 3. Detail Table {#sec:detail-table}

```{r Detail Table, eval = FALSE}
report_table(
  data_list = sl4.plot.data[["2D"]],
  
  pivot_col = list(Sector = "Sector"),
  group_by = list(
    Sector = list("Experiment", "Variable", "Region")),
  
  rename_cols = list("Experiment" = "Scenario"),
  
  total_column = FALSE,
  decimal = 6,
  subtotal_level = FALSE,
  repeat_label = FALSE,
  include_units = TRUE,

  var_name_by_description = FALSE,
  add_var_info = FALSE,
  add_group_line = FALSE,

  separate_sheet_by = NULL,
  export_table = TRUE,
  output_dir = output.folder,
  separate_file = FALSE,
  workbook_name = "Detail Table"
)
```

## 4. Decomposition Table {#sec:decomp-table}

```{r Decomposition Table, eval = FALSE}
report_table(
  data_list = har.plot.data,
  pivot_col = list(A = "COLUMN", 
                   E1 = "PRICES"),
  group_by = list(
    A = list("Experiment", "REG"), 
    E1 = list("Experiment", "REG", "COMM")
  ),
  rename_cols = list("REG" = "Region", 
                     "COMM" = "Sector",
                     "Experiment" = "Scenario"),
  
  total_column = TRUE,
  decimal = 6,
  subtotal_level = FALSE,
  repeat_label = FALSE,
  include_units = TRUE,

  var_name_by_description = FALSE,
  add_var_info = FALSE,
  add_group_line = FALSE,

  separate_sheet_by = NULL,
  export_table = TRUE,
  output_dir = output.folder,
  separate_file = FALSE,
  workbook_name = "Decomposition"
)
```

# Additional Utilities {#sec:additional-utilities}

## 1. Adding Unit and Description Columns {#sec:add-info}

If you manually import data or need to adjust the `"Description"` and
`"Unit"` columns, you can use the following command:

```{r Add Info, eval = FALSE}
mapping_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = c("qgdp", "EV", "ppriv"),
  Description = c("Real GDP Index", "Welfare Equivalents", "Consumer Price Index"),
  Unit = c("Percent", "million USD", "percent"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

datasets <- add_mapping_info(mapping_df, external_map = mapping_df, mapping = "Yes")
```

**Note:** Use `<?add_mapping_info>` to understand the meaning of `mapping`.


## 2. Converting Units and Values {#sec:converting-unit}

GTAP default values are typically reported in million USD, which may be too large for aesthetic plotting. This command converts units across all variables and data frames.

You can convert all units in a dataframe at once, but the *order must be defined correctly*:  

- `change_unit_from`: The original unit name in the `"Unit"` column to be changed.  
- `change_unit_to`: The new unit name to be recorded in the `"Unit"` column.  
- `adjustment`: The mathematical operation (`/`, `*`, `+`, or `-`) to transform the value.  

### Example Conversions:  
• Convert `million USD` to `billion USD` by dividing by 1,000.  
• Convert `percent` to `proportion` by dividing by 100.  

```{r Converting Unit, eval = FALSE}
datasets <- convert_units(change_unit_from = c("million USD", "percent"),
                          change_unit_to = c("billion USD", "proportion"),
                          adjustment = c("/1000", "/100"))
```


## 3. Renaming Columns and Data List Names {#sec:rename-column}

To modify column names across all datasets and/or rename data list names automatically—such as changing `REG` to `Region` or `COMM` to `Commodity`—use the following command:  

```{r Rename Column, eval = FALSE}
# Creating Mapping File
rename_col <- data.frame(
  old = c("REG", "COMM", "ACTS"),
  new = c("Region", "Commodity", "Activity")
  )

har.plot.data <- HARplus::rename_col(har.plot.data, rename_col)
```

💡 **Tip:** You can create this mapping dataframe in Excel and import it into R. The column names must be *"old"* and *"new"*.  

**Note:** The column names must be `"old"` and `"new"`. See `<?HARplus::rename_col>` for details.  


## 4. Renaming Values in a Dataframe {#sec:rename-value}

To automatically modify values in any column before plotting—such as renaming country names in the `REG` column (e.g., changing `"USA"` to `"United States"` or `"CHN"` to `"China"`)—use the following command:  

```{r Rename Value, eval = FALSE}
# Creating Mapping File
rename.region <- data.frame(
  ColumnName = "REG",
  OldName = c("USA", "CHN"),
  NewName = c("United States", "China"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

har.plot.data.rename <- rename_value(har.plot.data, mapping.file = rename.region)
```

💡 **Tip:** You can create this mapping dataframe in Excel and import it into R. The column names must be *"OldName"* and *"NewName"*, while `column_name` can be defined directly in the command. See `<?rename_value>` for details.  


# Manual Data Processing {#sec:manualdata}

This section is for non-GTAP models or manual data extraction for plotting. Follow these steps:

1. Use `"HARplus::load_sl4x"` or `"HARplus::load_harx"`, then `"HARplus::group_data_by_dims"` to structure the data in the required format.  

2. Filter each dataframe using standard R `data.frame` operations.  

3. Add the "Unit" and "Description" columns using `"add_mapping_info"` (the *"Unit"* column is required for plotting).  

```{r Manual Data Filtering, eval = FALSE}
# Step 1: Extracting Data
sl4data1 <- HARplus::load_sl4x(system.file("extdata", "EXP1.sl4", package = "HARplus"))
sl4data2 <- HARplus::load_sl4x(system.file("extdata", "EXP2.sl4", package = "HARplus"))
sl4data <- HARplus::get_data_by_dims(NULL, sl4data1, sl4data2, merge_data = TRUE)

# Step 2: Filtering Data using Dataframe and lapply
manual.data <- lapply(sl4data, function(x) {
  if (is.data.frame(x)) {
    x[x$REG %in% selected_regions & x$COMM %in% selected_sector & x$ACTS %in% selected_sector
      & x$Experiment %in% selected_exp , ]
  } else {
    x  
  }
})

# Step 3: Adding Unit and Description Column
manual.data <- add_mapping_info(manual.data, external_map = "/your/mapping.xlsx",
                                description_info = TRUE,
                                unit_info = TRUE)
```


# GTAP Macro Data Extraction {#sec:gtapmacro-dataextract}

Extract GTAP Macro variables from the *"Macros"* header in `.sl4` files using the following command:  

```{r GTAP Macro Data Extraction, eval = FALSE}
Macros <- gtap_macros_data(
  input_dir = input.folder,
  experiment_names = experiment,
  subtotal_level = FALSE
)
```

# Sample Data

Sample data used in this vignette is obtained from the GTAPv7 model
and utilizes publicly available data from the GTAP 9 database. For
more details, refer to the [GTAP Database Archive](https://www.gtap.agecon.purdue.edu/databases/archives.asp).
